checks: The revision preserves the exact statement and every argument after the new initial paragraph except for the change from citing strict quasiconcavity to citing the uniqueness proved locally. The remaining same-batch marked-transfer dependency is unchanged.

Through-cap volume is jointly continuous by dominated convergence since the limiting section has zero q-volume. Minimizing over the compact sphere gives an attained, continuous ordinary depth, hence a maximum on the compact body. Supporting planes and interior balls give zero boundary depth and positive interior depth, respectively.

At a minimizing through-cap at an interior mark the only section is proper with positive coarea. Formula (1) of 1269c554ca9a41b8 §2 with one fiber gives the two-sided derivative s·w·(g_section-y). Every small perturbed cap passes through y and has nonzero normal, so minimality makes the derivative vanish for all w and the section centroid equals y. The formula applies also for q=1, where the section is a singleton of positive H_0 mass.

If two distinct points attained the same maximum A, a minimizing through-cap at their midpoint would have volume at most A. With unequal endpoint thresholds, the larger threshold cap is strictly smaller because the intervening open slab meets the interior, contradicting the endpoint depth A. With equal endpoint thresholds, all three cap volumes coincide and are at least A by either endpoint depth, so the cap is minimizing through both endpoints. The single section centroid cannot equal both distinct marks. These cases establish the uniqueness needed for midpoint closure.

When n=0 the base is a singleton, Q contains it, k_Q=1 and the actual maximum is its intrinsic maximum A_z. Intrinsic Grünbaum gives the second bound and the strict antecedent is absent. Intrinsic halfspaces extend to ambient ones, while whole-plane traces cannot decrease the infimum.

For a positive convex combination of contacts with integer barycenter p, convexity puts the nonempty Minkowski sum inside K_p. Its direction space is the sum of the endpoint direction spaces: fix all but one summand to see containment of each endpoint direction, and use the converse inclusion from differences. Since every endpoint is q-dimensional and dim K_p≤q, all contributing direction spaces and the target direction space coincide. This argument is local to each integer interpolation.

Translations of the endpoint planes by origins with weighted mean the target origin preserve intrinsic volume and move the actual interpolated mark to its weighted translated mark. Over s affinely independent auxiliary bases in R^(s-1), s≥2, full-dimensional endpoint fibers make their convex hull full-dimensional. At the weighted auxiliary base the barycentric weights are unique, so its fiber is exactly the Minkowski combination. Joint depth-root concavity, then inclusion in K_p, gives the pointwise bound; s=1 needs no auxiliary body.

The positive affine majorant value at p equals the weighted sum of endpoint maxima roots. The pointwise bound and the definition of maximum squeeze the depth root at the interpolated mark to m_p=ℓ(p)>0. Thus Q is lattice-complete and uniqueness identifies g_p with the interpolated mark. This also proves conv(T) intersect (Z^n × R^d)=T, although the stated application only needs same-parity midpoints. Midpoints may change parity labels.

The parity theorem uses the actual lifted graph with weights A_z>0 and exactly the occupied base parity labels. Opposite proper caps through a deepest mark partition intrinsic volume up to a null hyperplane, giving A_z≤V_z/2<V_z. The face-weight strictness is transferred only for common direction space, and adding the remaining nonnegative fiber mass preserves either bound.

Taking the constant density 1 in the metronoid at mass V_z puts the intrinsic centroid in that metronoid. Its guaranteed raw depth γ_q V_z is at most A_z. Summation gives the second inequality with the same denominator k_Q.

For constant positive maxima, ℓ=A_*^(1/q) makes Q exactly the q-dimensional sites. Lower-dimensional fibers are H_q-null and distinct lifted fibers are disjoint. With k≤2^n and q≤d, the derivative of t log(t/(t+1)) is negative since log(1+1/t) is the integral of 1/(1+x) on [0,1/t] and exceeds the right-endpoint rectangle 1/(t+1). This gives the final γ_d bound.

Checked 4202609a15fa8f99 §§1 and 3–5, equations (2)–(4) and (6)–(7), against the original source and its committed SHA-256. The candidate accurately restricts the intrinsic theorem to q≥1 and strictness to common-direction contact fibers.

Uses the local cap derivative in §2, formula (1), with a singleton integer base, full-dimensional intrinsic q-body, nonzero normal and one proper section through an interior mark. Fix the base coefficient and vary the continuous normal by w and threshold by w·y. The nonproper trace condition is vacuous. The local formula, including its q=1 H_0 convention, is independent of the global projected-contact hypotheses.

Apply to the distinct contact bases with r=q, graph marks g_z in relative interiors and weights c_z=A_z≤V_z/2. The atomic center threshold is B_Q/k_Q. The strict assertion uses the common contact direction hypothesis and the strict minimal-face weight from the label theorem.

overlap.comparison: Gives ordinary depth-root concavity and maxima, but no lattice contact selection, graph center, or mixed-depth bound.
Supplies the sharp occupied-label atomic selection and face exception once lifted midpoint closure is checked; it neither proves that closure for deepest marks nor transfers to intrinsic mixed depth.

Proves the numerical Γ_d/2^n guarantee for equal positive volumes at a centroid. Equal positive raw ordinary maximal depths is a different hypothesis, and the present theorem further identifies deepest marks, arbitrary affine positive contacts and strictness.

The full-dimensional barycentric core lower bound could also pay the weak numerical bound once the new equality argument proves that each lattice contact mark belongs to every barycentric core of the singleton deepest marks. Its direct unconditional special case assumes equal positive volumes; it lacks the intrinsic and strict conclusions.

Uses a different contact selection at energy maximizers inside a mixed-depth superlevel set. It pays retained volume through centroids, whereas the current theorem uses an arbitrary affine majorant of ordinary depth roots and pays actual ordinary maxima at deepest marks.

initial_review.readability: The proof cites strict quasiconcavity and marked transfer in words rather than repeating their IDs. At n=0 the first inequality is equality and the face exception is automatic.
initial_review.summary: Intrinsic Minkowski comparison at every integer convex combination forces closure of the positive contact bases and preservation of the lifted deepest marks. The occupied-parity graph center gives the asserted contact mass and, in a common direction, the strict alternative. The equal-maximum case retains all measured mass.
